call_points.text: Overseas EBITDA margin fell to 5.1% on lower services contribution; recovery expected from Q2 for KBL.
Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 13.7% from 12.8%; consolidated margin lower due to SPP UK.
FY27 capex expected to equal depreciation, used for modernisation, debottlenecking and quality.
Nuclear primary circuit pumps orders close to ₹70 Cr in Q1; secondary circuit about ₹40 Cr.
Price hikes of about 10% taken since January, expected to cover raw material cost increases.
Inventory rose as foundry modernisation left orders half-completed; management expects improvement from this month.
Rodelta losses widened on delayed execution; management expects improvement in the next two quarters.

penalties.details: The Company had filed Annual Secretarial Compliance Report (ASCR) for the Financial Year ended March 31, 2025, in XBRL format, within prescribed time. However, the same filing in PDF format was missed out at BSE. Please note that the Company had filed both XBRL and PDF format for the ASCR in NSE within prescribed time. In view of this, BSE had imposed a fine of Rs. 50,000 (Plus GST). The Company rectified the inadvertent error by filing ASCR in PDF format on the same day, upon intimation by BSE on June 26, 2025 and filed waiver application for withdrawal of notice and penalty imposed thereto by BSE. However, with reference to email communication received from BSE dated June 05, 2026, the aforesaid waiver application was not approved and levy of aforesaid penalty was upheld by BSE. Accordingly, the said penalty of Rs. 50,000 (plus GST) was paid to BSE on June 11, 2026.

penalties.details: The Company has received an email dated August 10, 2026, from NSE Limited (“NSE”), seeking clarification on observation of non-compliance with Regulation 19(1)(c) of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, in relation to the composition of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee (“NRC”) as reported in the Corporate Governance Report for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. The Company responded on August 12, 2026, confirming that it had inadvertently interpreted the requirement of at least two-thirds of the members of the NRC being Independent Directors as requiring a minimum of three Independent Directors in a five-member Committee and appropriate corrective action would be undertaken to ensure compliance. Further, the Company had promptly initiated corrective measures by re-constitution NRC strictly as per Reg. 19 w.e.f. August 14, 2026. The Company submitted the response to NSE on August 14, 2026, stating that the non-compliance was inadvertent and without any mala fide intent and that corrective action had been initiated upon receipt of the observations from the Stock Exchange. In view of the above, NSE in its notice dated August 25, 2026 levied a penalty of Rs. 87,320/-. Accordingly, the penalty of Rs. 87,320/- was paid to NSE on September 01, 2026.
